text:
If you've got outdoor plans today, front-load them, because the back half of this one turns messy fast. Expect a partly sunny start near 83, but showers and thunderstorms build in through the afternoon, and the forecasters are flagging an isolated flash flood risk as this system slows down tonight into Monday. That's not just NWS caution either, the European model is running much wetter than the American one today, and I'd bet on the wetter side given how the discussion reads. Rain odds jump to 90% overnight with a soaking half inch possible, so tonight's really the main event, not today.

On the lake, a wind advisory is up, south winds 15 to 25 knots with waves 2 to 3 feet this afternoon, building seas that'll only calm after dark. If you're on the water, be off well before those afternoon storms fire. Monday stays unsettled with showers likely much of the day and a high near 80, before things finally quiet down Tuesday. Good window for outdoor plans is really just this morning, call it before noon.
